author: Claude
candidate_edge: A single session-open-gap fade signal per weekday per symbol on AUDJPY and GBPJPY, each anchored to its OWN native Asia-session liquidity handoff rather than to USDJPY's Tokyo-AM breakout window: AUDJPY at the Sydney/Tokyo open (21:00-22:00 UTC) and GBPJPY at the Tokyo/London liquidity handoff (06:00-07:00 UTC). Trigger is mean-reversion (fade an outsized session-open gap/spike back toward the prior session's range), the mechanical opposite of Balke's breakout-with-stop-bracket, addressing the task's requirement for 'a different trigger than the Balke stop bracket'.
confidence: Low. This is the weakest-grounded of the three hypotheses: every measured breakout/momentum-style configuration on these pairs in the frozen screen is net-negative, which motivates trying a different trigger family but does not itself provide positive evidence for mean-reversion -- there is no measured fade-style configuration on AUDJPY/GBPJPY in the current evidence to anchor an E[R] prior on, so the E[R] prior here is a bare structural assumption (mean-reversion in an illiquid session with a magnitude filter) rather than a scaled-up measured analogue as in H-V1/H-V2.
confounders: AUDJPY and GBPJPY are both JPY-denominated; any JPY-strength/weakness macro shock could drive correlated moves on both legs on the same day, and both would also share tail risk with the existing 13213 USDJPY sleeve if fitted into the same book -- falsification criterion 5 below is designed specifically to catch this.

A fade-the-gap mechanism is exactly the failure mode that a genuine trend day punishes hardest (fading a real breakout into a continuing move) -- this is a real and known risk of mean-reversion triggers, not merely a modeling nuance, and the magnitude filter's calibration is unproven.

AUDJPY's 21:00-22:00 UTC window and GBPJPY's 06:00-07:00 UTC window are both low-average-liquidity relative to London/NY hours; the .DWX tester's zero-spread modeling (FTMO_PORTFOLIO_GAP_CURRENT.md section 1b) is likely MORE optimistic here than for London-hours FX majors, because real-world spread widening in thin sessions is larger than in liquid ones.

No measured fire count exists yet for a fade-style trigger on these instruments in this specific window; the density prior below is a pure structural inference and carries more uncertainty than H-V1/H-V2's.
observations: Every measured breakout/momentum-continuation configuration on AUDJPY/GBPJPY/EURJPY/CHFJPY in the frozen Q02 screen is net-negative (6 configurations, all R_bd < 0, see baseline_extract.json). Separately, the 41484 fan-out already falsified transplanting the Balke breakout-with-stop-bracket trigger AND window onto AUDJPY/GBPJPY specifically (AUDJPY +0.005R flat, GBPJPY -0.001R flat). Two independent lines of evidence therefore point away from a breakout-family trigger on these pairs, which is the direct motivation for testing a mean-reversion/fade trigger instead, at each pair's own native session anchor rather than USDJPY's Tokyo-AM window.
proposed_mechanism: AUDJPY and GBPJPY are crosses whose 'home' liquidity structure is not the same Tokyo-AM window that defines USDJPY's Balke edge: AUDJPY's natural session anchor is the Sydney/Tokyo liquidity open (a thin-book handoff prone to overshoot-and-revert gaps), and GBPJPY's is the Tokyo/London handoff (a different thin-book transition). In a genuinely thin, low-average-liquidity window, an outsized session-open gap is structurally more likely to be a liquidity-driven overshoot than a sustained information-driven move, which is the opposite economic logic from a liquid-session breakout (Balke's Tokyo-AM USDJPY edge, or H-V1's London-open EURUSD/GBPUSD edge) -- a fade-the-gap mechanism, not a breakout-follow-through mechanism, is the natural trigger for each pair's own thin-liquidity session.
